newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee settles firmer, but off highs.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee settles firmer, but off highs.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended moderately higher in technically driven trade Wednesday, buoyed by speculative buying, market sources said.
But steady selling by producers prevented the active March contract from reaching buy stops placed above chart resistance at 113.00 cents a lb, prompting some speculators to shed their long postions.
Most-active March ended 0.95 higher at 111.35 after trading from 112.80 to 109.75. December rose 0.30 to 118.50, while the rest finished 0.45 to 0.50 firmer.
The widely watched December/March switch narrowed to 7.15 cents from 7.80 cents at Tuesday's close.
Players continued to roll the December contract forward ahead of first notice day Nov 19, traders said.
Heavy rollover by speculators on Tuesday knocked December's open interest down 1,930 lots to 6,553 lots. March open interest rose by 1,372 lots to 14,656 lots.
Meanwhile, CSCE said earlier this week U.S. certified coffee stocks fell to a mere 333 bags, or the equivalent of about one lot of coffee.
Traders said tight nearby availability would continue to provide supportive fundamental background for the market.

They await monthly inventory data from the Green Coffee Association of New York due after the close on Friday. Most traders expected the stock report to show a decline of between 200,000 and 300,000 60-kg bags in October, although one trader predicted the drawdown could be as large as 500,000 bags.
In September, supplies of green coffee in U.S. warehouses fell by 205,000 bags to 1,611,000 bags, their lowest level since the GCA began charting inventories in January, 1988.
On the charts, near-term resistance for March coffee continued to be noted at 113.00, while support was pegged at 108.40.
The day's volume was moderate, at an estimated 7,409 lots.
